text.p: The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Friday that the combined chemical and petroleum industry output was expected to grow 9.5-10.5 percent in 1996 to reach S$22 billion.

In a statement, the EDB said that petrochemical output alone fell 10.5 percent in value terms owing to "sluggish product prices" during 1996. The statement did not provide the overall value of output.
"Prices of key petrochemicals such a polyolefins and paraxylene fell by 10 to 20 percent globally compared to 1995 resulting in weak margins," the statement said.
The petroleum sector alone rebounded strongly in 1996 to show a growth in the value of its output of 14.5 percent over 1995. Figures were not provided.
"However, thinner refining margins due to the increase in suppy from new refineries in the region have placed strong competitive pressures on Singapore refiners," the EDB said.
